recipes.name: Okra and Tomatoes
ingredients_raw: 1 pound frozen okra, thawed and sliced

steps.text: Place bacon in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium-high heat until evenly browned and crisp. Drain; crumble bacon onto a plate and set aside.
Add okra, onion, pepper, and celery to the pan; sauté until tender. Add tomatoes, salt, and pepper; cook and stir until tomatoes are heated through.

raw_recipe.headline: Okra and Tomatoes
raw_recipe.description: Okra and tomatoes are sautéed with onion, green pepper, and celery in this easy recipe; garnish with crumbled bacon for a tasty side dish.

review.reviewBody: I've made this a couple of times now. The first time I followed the recipe and it turned out great. The second time, I found I didn't have any canned tomatos, but I had a few roma's , so I diced those up and added a little tomato sauce. It still turned out perfect. Every one at my house loves it either way. I sometimes add a little Creole seasoning for a little extra kick. This is one of those recipes that's just real hard to goof up. Thanks for posting a great recipe!

Amazing!!! Here's how I spiced it up my own way and made it an entree. In the bacon fat (i left it all) I fried a 1/4 tsp each of caraway seed, fennel seed, and mustard seed. Before frying the onion, okra, celery and added 3 large cloves of minced garlic and a diced jalapeno. After that cooked through I added roma tomatoes that I chopped and smashed with my hands and let marinade for 30 min in the following; 1/2 tsp of fresh grated ginger, 1/2 a lime fresh squeezed plus pulp, 1/4 tsp of lemon garlic seasoning, and 1/4 teaspoon seafood seasoning like old bay. After the tomatoes cooked and released enough water to make it soupy I added a half pound of catfish nuggets that seasoned with the same as the tomatoes; lime, lemon garlic, old bay or mccormick Chesapeake bay and a pinch of ginger. I also added the fresh grated black pepper, sea salt flakes and some ground and crushed red pepper for some heat since I like things spicy. I served it over rice and found that if you like it saltier, soy sauce was a great addition. Great with a glass of South African Pinotage.

Made this according to directions and it was delicious. We make something similar by frying bacon and then sautéing onions and bell pepper. Then I add a quart of home canned tomatoes, probably 2 T. soy sauce, 2 T. port wine and let it simmer down some. Sometimes I add 1 t. sesame oil for a different flavor. Always add a shake or 2 of Cajun seasoning. Really don't have a recipe, just what you like. Anyway, let it simmer down a bit more and take your bacon (usually about 4 slices) and crumble it on top just before serving. Hubby and I love it.

My father made this when I was growing up, it was his mother's recipe. I continue to make it and find it goes wonderfully with fish or chicken and rice. I use items straight from the garden and put it all in a casserole dish and bake in a hot oven until veggies tender and brown around edges. Although bacon grease is traditional, and wonderful, olive oil works well. Thanks for posting a great old southern recipe.

I grew up with a mother that was from the south and okra was a good staple in our household and it was cooked many different ways, this was one of the ways she cooked it but also in a cast-iron skillet with cornmeal and egg. I’ve always loved okra and when I cooked us I cooked it for a friend who never had okra ever, they loved it! This is a very easy recipe To follow and it comes out quite tasty, I did add fresh garlic and a jalapeño pepper finely chopped to give it a little heat it was delicious???

Husband has a new vegetable love. The bacon as a seasoning is definitely Southern, and okra grows like kudzu down here. You can stretch this into a one dish meal with sweet corn, ground beef and rice. Just adjust the seasonings to taste. Great low budget meal.

I used okra and peeled, seeded tomatoes from my garden, added 1 jalapeno (we love dishes with a little heat) and doubled the recipe. With only adding the jalapeno to the base recipe, the flavor of this recipe was outstanding.
I did this recipe and it was great, I did add a little step by searing andouille sausage after the bacon then everything else by instructions. I have 5 kids and even the picky eater enjoyed this

This is a great side dish that hits the spot! I made a few additions to make it a little more like my Moms. I added 1 tsp of Cajun seasoning, 1.5 tsp of sugar, 1.5 tsp onion powder, and 1 tsp of white vinegar. I served it for friends this evening and they loved it!

I hate okra. I hate it less after this recipe, which is really saying something. We used fresh tomatoes from the garden (8 roma and 3 yellow heirloom) instead of canned, because we had a ton of them - and for seasoning I used a Mrs Dash spicy pepper blend. I felt like it needed a lot of salt, which must come naturally if using canned tomatoes. There was still that stringy snotty slime essence, but, this is a REALLY great way to eat okra without deep frying it. Served with a side of Andouille sausage, over rice - next time, I'll cut the sausage up and cook it in the stew. Yes, I said next time! I'm surprised, too.

Simple and forgiving recipe. Like many people have said, a little seasoning brings it up a level. I added paprika, extra garlic, and cayenne pepper. A little splash of apple cider vinegar at the end makes all the difference as well. Delicious served over rice.

Everything is here that I like in mine and the out come was good this time. But I always want a recipe that is consistent. I am wondering if you have the weight of the fresh vegetables you use so I could try it from that?

I used sliced frozen okra & petite diced tomatoes with onions green pepper & celery in one can. I used stored bacon drippings, and used previously cooked bacon bits. I seasoned generously with Paul Prudhomme vegetable magic along with salt & pepper.
Not a fan of Okra but my wife loves it. I made this for her on Mother's day. She said she got a little teary eyed because this hit so close to home. I even liked it.

I just used bacon bits I had on hand and sauteed them with fresh tomatoes instead of canned and used jalapeno peppers instead of green. I wanted a little more kick to it. Everything else is per the recipe. It's delicious.
